messages:
Maria R.: quick heads-up: hit a billing gotcha in canary where runtime retried to a smaller model and both token counts landed in the ledger. curious if we prefer dedupe at ingest or a post-ingest finalizer.
Sam K.: are the two events identical except model_id? or different event_ids?
Maria R.: same request_id, different model_id and event_id. one marked status=partial, later status=complete. our current charge join uses (request_id, model_id) so both become charges.
Alex T.: my vote is finalizer: ingest emits raw_event, provisional_charge; finalizer consumes all raw_events for request_id within a short window, picks canonical outcome, emits finalized_charge + adjustments. handles retries and partials.
Jamal P.: agreed. ingestion-only dedupe can't reason about partial vs eventual success. finalizer can apply priority rules: prefer successful over partial, prefer lowest-latency model? we should document priority precedence.
Sam K.: main downside is billing latency. ops/product will complain if dashboards lag. can we have provisional flows that are clearly labeled?
Maria R.: yes: provisional_charge {provisional: true, provisional_id}, finalized_charge references provisional_id and has canonical_charge_id. dashboards show provisional until finalized.
Alex T.: technical detail: finalizer must be idempotent and handle out-of-order arrivals. plan: partition by request_id, buffer for watermark=20s, then apply deterministic selection (status > success, max event_ts if tie). late-arrivals produce corrections.
Jamal P.: also need canonical_charge_id in every record so we can link before/after. auditors want raw events + final choice. archive raw_events to s3 with redaction flag to strip logits/embeddings.
Maria R.: costing question: if fallback was cheaper but produced more tokens and increased bill, product insists on charging executed model. but show requested_model and routing_reason in invoice metadata.
Sam K.: schema change checklist then: add fields to charge event: canonical_charge_id, provisional_id, provisional_bool, requested_model_id, executed_model_id, routing_reason, redaction_flags, raw_event_uri.
Alex T.: and add event_type enum: provisional | finalized | adjustment | audit_raw. also include billing_version for future schema migration.
infra-bot: alert: metering topic throughput spike detected 12:12 UTC; auto-throttle engaged. check #eng-infra. :rotating_light:
ops-oncall: noted. finalizer can run in shards with rate limits; if too slow we'll back-pressure provisional emits to protect the topic.
Maria R.: one more edge: streaming responses that produce tokens incrementally. we may receive multiple token events for same request while model still streaming. finalizer should sum tokens by stream_id and prefer the last `stream_state=complete` event.
Jamal P.: good call. add stream_id and sequence_number to raw events. finalizer aggregates per (request_id, stream_id).
Sam K.: incremental rollout approach: 1) add provisional emits (no change to billing) 2) deploy finalizer in canary (sample X% requests) 3) enable finalization adjustments in ledger 4) audit and compare provisional vs final for a week 5) flip default to finalized charges.
Alex T.: also add an operator playbook for long-tail finalization >1min: manual review flag + automated revert to provisional if missing evidence.
Maria R.: I'll draft RFC with the delta schema + example messages and rollout plan. will include sample canonical_charge JSON and an adjustment example. tagging @Alex T. @Jamal P.
ops-oncall: thanks — if finalizer increases consumer lag we will throttle provisional emits automatically. keep us posted. :thumbsup:
